svg.title: How an audit runs: scripts discover, models judge, every report is validated
svg.desc: The security-audit pipeline as nine phases, each split into what deterministic scripts do and what a model does. Phase 0 Scope: env_check, detect_stack and questions; the lead asks depth, report language, focus and formats. Phase 1 Recon and intel: platform_inventory, threat_intel in the background against public advisory feeds, repo_digest, route_map and agent_config_audit; the recon-mapper subagent (Sonnet, medium) maps the attack surface. Phase 2 Sweep: sensitive_sweep and peek; the data model is read by the lead or the sensitive-data lane. Phase 3 Scanners: run_scanners with eight pinned scanners in the background, then normalize_findings with rule-based auto-refute; no model. Phase 4 Lanes: lane_pack; lane-reviewer subagents in parallel, Sonnet, Opus on design lanes at Deep. Phase 5 Triage and verify: collect_lanes; the finding-verifier tries to refute each candidate. Phase 6 Register: new_finding writes one file per root cause. Phase 7 Report: build_report, validate_findings, render_html, render_xlsx and prune_work; the lead writes the narrative and translator subagents produce other languages. Phase 8, only on request: re-scan with the same scanner digests and close a finding only when it no longer reproduces and the rule still fires. Outputs: findings per language and repo, and Markdown, HTML and Excel reports.

g.text: How an audit runs: scripts discover, models judge, every report is validated
Phases 0 to 8 left to right. Scanners and the advisory match start early and run in the background while recon and the sweep continue. Nothing is written inside the audited repo.
one file per root cause, the same
ids and anchors in every language
HTML: search, filters, deep links, CSV
Quick runs recon, up to three lanes and the
verification inline in the main session.
Standard and Deep hand them to named
subagents with read-only tools and turn caps.
The audit folder sits beside the repo, never in it.
